study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissecting heterogeneity in major depressive disorder via normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Use normative modeling of healthy controls to quantify individual deviations in ROI-wise degree centrality from rs-fMRI, and subtype MDD patients via k-means on deviation profiles; relate subtype patterns to symptoms and cognition.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) accounting for site-specific means and variances; common prior distribution across multiple sites; site-specific yet interrelated parameter estimation; preserves meaningful site-related variations while accommodating signal and noise variability in multisite data; age and sex as fixed effects
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: To minimize the impact of site-related variability on subsequent results, hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality as a function of age and sex for each brain region... HBR allows for the imposition of a common prior distribution across multiple sites to estimate site-specific yet interrelated means and variances, thus accommodating signal and noise variability in multisite data while preserving meaningful site-related variations

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of rs-fMRI degree centrality revealed two MDD subtypes with opposing deviation patterns between unimodal (VIS/SMN) and transmodal (LIM/FPN/DMN) networks, accompanied by distinct cognitive associations and clinical differences.
